$comment: THE E1 BOUNDARY-LINT BACKLOG — criterion D7.
D7: "The E1 86-violation backlog is closed, or every remaining item is a dated deferral
carrying an OD id — and the count is DERIVED FROM THE LINT RUN, never restated from
this contract."
SO THE NUMBER 86 APPEARS NOWHERE AS AN AUTHORITY IN THIS FILE, and neither does 54. The gate
tools/p2/gates/e1-backlog.mjs RUNS the lint that produced the backlog —
ESLINT_USE_FLAT_CONFIG=true eslint --config .eslintrc.boundaries.js src
— the same command, the same five rules R1..R5, against the current tree, and counts what comes
back. This file does not say how many there are. It says what each one IS.
WHY THIS LINT AND NOT THE §9.4 GATE. Both police the same five boundaries. When the §9.4 rules
in tools/p2/lib/boundary-rules.mjs first ran clean they printed `5 rules, 0 violations` while
this lint, on the same tree, found 58. The successor was WEAKER than the predecessor whose
backlog D7 exists to close, and its green would have covered every one of them. The two are now
both required: D5's gate proves the §9.4 rules find nothing, and this gate proves the ORIGINAL
rules find nothing UNACCOUNTED FOR. A finding that matches no disposition below is a hard
failure, and a disposition that matches nothing is a stale entry and also a hard failure.
DISPOSITIONS ARE PREDICATES, NOT LINE NUMBERS. A register of `file:line` pairs rots on the next
edit and then gets regenerated by whoever is annoyed by it, which is how a backlog becomes a
rubber stamp. Each entry below states a rule, a file pattern and a message pattern, and the gate
reports how many live findings each one actually covers.

lint.adoptedBy: e3a5fbf — T2: adopt E1 boundary-lint diagnostic into the integration branch

dispositions.why: 100 IS THE DEFINITION OF 'PERCENT', not a rate anyone chose. Every site is `x / 100` or `x * 100` converting between a percentage and a fraction, or `Math.round(v * 100) / 100` rounding to two decimals. Moving it to config would imply a product could set percent to mean something other than per hundred. The test this campaign applies — could this number, if wrong, tell a user something false about their money? — answers no: if it were wrong the arithmetic would not be a different rate, it would not be percentage arithmetic at all, and every test would fail at once.

parseAmount TURNS A TEXT FIELD INTO A NUMBER AND BOUNDS-CHECKS IT. It strips separators and the shekel sign, refuses non-finite input, and compares against MONETARY_MIN_ILS and MONETARY_MAX_ILS — which already live in src/config/financial.ts. It computes nothing: no rate, no fee, no derived figure. A screen that could not parse its own input would have to send raw strings to an engine, which moves the parsing rather than removing it, and puts unvalidated text one layer closer to the arithmetic.

A SORT COMPARATOR, NOT A CALCULATION SITE. The line is `const commissionDifference = a.commission - b.commission` inside `.sort()`, used only for its sign to order rows cheapest-first. It produces no value any user sees and no value any other code reads. The rule is right to look at subtraction on a field called commission; a reader looking at it sees a comparator.

A TEST FIXTURE REGISTER, NOT A RUNTIME DATA READ. render-fixtures.json lists which screens the render harness mounts and with what props; it carries no card, rate or fee. It exists because the harness must DERIVE its screen population rather than hand-list it, and it is recorded as DEVIATION D-3 in campaign-p2/DEVIATIONS.md. R3 protects provenance on reference reads at runtime; nothing here reaches runtime.

ENGINE SCORING BANDS, AND P2 MAY NOT TOUCH ENGINE ARITHMETIC. These are the weights and band boundaries inside cardRoleEngine and cashflowRadar — `score >= 75`, `score += 20`. They are genuine product decisions and they do belong in config eventually. Moving them now means editing the arithmetic of engines this campaign is explicitly forbidden to change: P3 owns the engine rewrite, and a constant relocated by P2 and re-derived by P3 is two answers to one question, which is the defect the relocation would be trying to prevent.
dispositions.odMeaning: OD-32 adopted P2_COMPLETION_CONTRACT.md including §9's out-of-scope list; 'no engine arithmetic' is a hard prohibition of this campaign under that adoption.

dispositions.why: A BOUND QUOTED IN PROSE — the same mirror already recorded in tools/p2/financial-literals.allow.json under $knownMirror, and recorded there before this backlog was re-run. Each site is a translated sentence that states a percentage the rules also compute, so the two can drift and nothing would notice. The repair is interpolation into translated copy, which needs the single money formatter that criterion A7 builds in Phase 5. Rewriting the strings now, without the formatter meant to render them, would mean touching them twice.

dispositions.why: THE STORAGE DRIVER REACHES MODULES THAT ARE NOT THE VAULT. This is real and it is criterion B3's subject: the store split, which decides which module may own persistence and how the vault boundary is drawn. locale.ts and authContext.tsx were the two sites at adoption. P4 onboarding added useFinishSetupStore.ts for skip/dismiss flags — the same unencrypted-preferences class, not a new driver. Repairing it here would mean guessing that split in Phase 3 and then meeting the criterion that defines it in Phase 10.

dispositions.why: BUILD CONFIGURATION, NOT A REFERENCE READ. R3 exists so every reference read carries its provenance, tier and lastUpdated — a rate, a fee, a card. identity.json holds the display name, the bundle id and a storage namespace. None of it is a fact about anybody money, none of it has a provenance to lose, and A10 requires it to be ONE file readable by two consumers: the app through the bundler, and Expo config loader in plain Node before TypeScript exists. That is why it cannot live under src/config/** with the other constants, and why R3 sees it.

THE MODULE CRITERION B3 DESIGNATES AS THE DRIVER'S OWNER. R3 exists so a reference read goes through one place that carries provenance, tier and lastUpdated — and this IS that place for pack data. B3 requires SQLCipher-class SQLite for imported pack tables and the store-split gate asserts that exactly one module opens it, that the vault never imports SQLite, and that this module never imports MMKV. The original R3 was written when src/authority/** was the only sanctioned data owner; B3 named a second, and the pack store is it.

THE PREDECESSOR LINT WAS WRITTEN BEFORE THE PERMITTED DIRECTORY EXISTED. Its R3 names src/authority/ as the only place that may import a JSON dataset, because src/data/adapter/** did not exist when it was adopted — the adapter seam is criterion D1 and landed in Phase 7. SMARTCARD_APP_ENGINEERING_SPEC §9.4 says NOTHING OUTSIDE data/adapter/** may import a pack file, a raw JSON dataset or the DB driver, and this file is inside it. The successor rule (tools/p2/lib/boundary-rules.mjs, rule 3) already carries the permitted set and reports zero. AND THIS IS NOT A DATASET. It is the adapter package's own metadata block, read for smartcard.builtFromCommit — the one fact the adapter does not export from its code, and the load-bearing half of D1's pin, since two builds can carry one adapterVersion and different behaviour. It holds no rate, no fee and no provenance to lose, which is the property R3 exists to protect. Removing the import would not move the fact anywhere; it would delete the app's ability to notice at runtime that it is running against an adapter nobody reviewed.

THE PREDECESSOR LINT CALLS EVERY MODULE UNDER THE SEAM A PACK MODULE, because src/authority/ was the boundary directory when it was adopted and src/data/adapter/** did not exist. But a seam nothing may import is not a seam: D2 forbids anything outside data/adapter/** from importing A PACK FILE, A RAW JSON DATASET OR THE DB DRIVER, and reaching the boundary THROUGH its modules is the arrangement that makes that possible rather than a violation of it. crossSet.ts is the narrowest case there is: three string states, a ReferenceResolution type, and a resolver that holds no pack bytes, opens no file and cannot throw. A component rendering an absent cross-set reference has to name that type. This disposition is scoped to the crossSet module BY NAME rather than to the directory: a component importing fsPackReader, which pulls node:fs into a React Native bundle, would still be UNACCOUNTED here and would also fail the node-apis-absent gate, which walks the runtime graph from index.js and App.tsx.

THE SAME REASON AS ALLOW-CROSSSET-RESOLVER, AND ONE MORE. The predecessor lint calls every module under src/data/adapter/** a pack module because src/authority/ was the boundary directory when it was adopted; a seam nothing may import is not a seam, and D2 forbids importing A PACK FILE, A RAW JSON DATASET OR THE DB DRIVER, not the boundary's own modules. The additional reason here is that conflictRenderPlan.ts imports the adapter AS A TYPE ONLY, so it is ERASED at runtime and carries no pack data, no adapter code and no Node API into a React Native bundle. That erasure is why it exists as a separate module at all: the render suite failed with 'Cannot find module @babel/runtime/helpers/interopRequireDefault' when the component reached the adapter's runtime through a file: junction resolving outside the app root. Scoped to the module BY NAME: a component importing conflictRender.ts, which does load the adapter, stays UNACCOUNTED here.

THE WIZARD READS THE SHIPPED CATALOG FROM THE SANCTIONED DIRECTORY. D2 (lint-boundaries rule 3) permits only data/adapter/** to import a pack file. The predecessor lint still names src/authority/** as the adapter, so catalogSearch and clubResolver are accounted here rather than the lint being widened. Screens never open pack.json; they ask src/authority/addCardCatalog.ts, which re-exports these modules. Direct JSON rather than @smartcard/data-authority-adapter keeps the add-card render harness free of the adapter package's Node graph.

THE DEV PROBE SEAM IS INSIDE THE SANCTIONED DIRECTORY. The WP-7.1 device-evidence harness reads the shipped catalog and fx-rates packs from src/data/adapter/devProbeInputs.ts - the directory every P2 boundary rule names as the only permitted pack reader. The lint predates the P2 rename and still permits only src/authority/**, so the location is accounted here rather than the lint being widened. D2 itself (adapter-consumption, lint-boundaries rule 3) passes this file.

__DEV__-ONLY DIAGNOSTICS CONSUMING THE SEAM, NOT THE PACKS. The probe imports the adapter seam module and the two BOI-lane modules - it never opens a pack file or a driver. Its only product-side sibling is the Settings row that reaches it, registered under __DEV__ so release builds carry neither route nor module.

TYPE-ONLY IMPORT THROUGH THE RE-EXPORT SEAM. The engines need the shipped FxRate type; importing the package directly would breach D2 (a second importer of the pack boundary), so they import the type through src/data/adapter/vocabulary.ts, which re-exports the pipeline-owned definition unchanged. No value logic crosses this line.

A TEST FIXTURE HELPER, NOT A RUNTIME DATA READ. one-number.test.ts uses the shared EXPECTED_DATASET_ID pin while proving no two call sites produce different numbers over the full universe; nothing is read from a pack through this import.

UNIT CONVERSION, NOT A RATE. fxPercent arrives as a percentage and is applied as a fraction; multiplying by 100 is the percentage-point-to-fraction identity inside the engine that owns it, with its citation on the same line.
ENGINE-OWNED CITED CONSTANT. Advisory small-amount threshold whose home is the engine by the P3 contract (G11 admits declared, cited engine constants); the citation sits on the declaration line.
SCORE NORMALISATION ARITHMETIC, NOT A THRESHOLD. x100 converts a ratio to the 0-100 scale the scoring engine returns; it tunes nothing.

ENGINE-OWNED DEFAULTS THE CALLER OVERRIDES. The verdict load ratios are inputs with these values as documented fallbacks (evaluatePurchaseVerdict accepts safeLoadRatio/hardLoadRatio); the defaults live beside the threshold math they parameterise, per the P3 contract.

A COMPARISON TO WHOLENESS, NOT A THRESHOLD. `discountPercent === 100` asks whether the fee is fully waived; 100 is the definition of a whole percentage, not a rate or a cut-off this app chose. Moving it to config/** would put the number 100 in the file that holds the app's opinions about prudence, where a reader would reasonably look for a policy and find an arithmetic identity. Same reasoning as ALLOW-FXPERCENT-BY-100.

IT IS A SHARED VOCABULARY, NOT A PACK READ. `benefitLookup` reads no pack: it holds ISSUER_DATABASE_KEYS and the club lookup keyed by displayName, and its own docblock states why it lives in data — 'engines may import from src/data while B1 forbids a surface from value-importing src/engines, making data the only place both callers can read from.' Routing this through src/authority/ would give the engine and Card DNA two doors onto one vocabulary, which is the desynchronisation the module was created to prevent. Same shape as ALLOW-VOCABULARY-TYPE-IMPORTS.

A LAYOUT COORDINATE, NOT A RATE. `${ratio * 100}%` turns an engine ratio into the CSS percentage React Native needs to POSITION a threshold tick along the bar; the number it produces is an x-offset and is never shown, compared or carried into any calculation. The ratio itself comes from load.thresholds and is not restated here. It was written for the RTL repair (D-032), which is why it appears now: the tick used to be placed with `start`, which is direction-blind in this app.

dispositions.message: financial arithmetic on 'foreignTransactionFee' performed here, outside src/engines/
dispositions.why: A UNIT CONVERSION FOR A DISPLAY STRING, and it feeds nothing. `String(fee * 100)` renders a stored fraction as the percentage Card DNA section A's fx-commission row shows; the result is a string, is never read back as a number, and no engine consumes it. NOTED AND NOT HIDDEN: this is a SECOND place the app converts between fraction and percent by hand, and the first is the subject of Owner question OQ-P5-003 — `formatPercent` appends a percent sign WITHOUT multiplying, so ratios render a hundred times too small. Whoever settles OQ-P5-003 should read this entry: one convention would delete both.

TEST SUPPORT, AND THE CRITERION REQUIRES THE READ. These two modules build the group-A agreement population, and criterion A6 demands it be DERIVED: 'the population the agreement properties run over is derived from the navigation declaration and the shipped packs, never hand-listed, and a check over zero surfaces fails.' The card set comes from currentCatalogProducts(), which is the door P4's wizard already uses onto the shipped catalog and is itself allowed at ALLOW-WIZARD-CATALOG-PACK-READ. Satisfying R3 by hand-listing cards here would break A6 and reintroduce the maintained 'everything' list that P1 shipped four of. Neither file is in the app bundle. Same shape as ALLOW-RENDER-FIXTURE, one directory over.
